These plans will be executed autonomously by ralphex, task by task, with little human steering

the wrong thing and looks like it succeeded.

Weigh points by that standard.

## What I most want to know

1. **Is the central architectural bet sound?** The bet is that keeping `pixel-core` and replacing
   only its tty layer is cheaper than dropping it. That bet rests on a count of unix-API references
   per module. A reference count is a proxy for portability, and proxies fail. Is there a module in
   the "19 with zero hits" column that will not in fact build or behave on Windows — a path
   assumption, a threading assumption, a font or clipboard dependency, an unwrap on something
   unix-shaped? `arboard` and `fontdue` are worth a look specifically.

2. **Does the plan's task ordering actually work?** Each task claims to be independently completable
   with tests passing before the next begins. Find the task that cannot be, or whose tests cannot
   mean anything until a later task lands.

3. **Is the first-frame-on-screen milestone (Task 8) reachable where it sits?** It is placed before
   interactive input and before the shm path deliberately. If something earlier is missing for it to
   work, that is the single most valuable thing to find.

   plan's Task 10 depends on a spec file the agwinterm plan produces at its Task 1. Is that enough,

# Project conventions

winterm-browser is a Windows-native port. Its conventions are inherited from two places, and where
they disagree with general taste, they win.

## From upstream terminal-browser, which is being vendored

- Rust: `cargo nextest run --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo fmt --all --check`. Warnings are errors.
- `pixel-core` lints deny undocumented unsafe blocks and warn on `unsafe_code` crate-wide. A port
  that reaches for Win32 will need unsafe; it must be documented to build.
- TypeScript packages test with `node --test`.
- 37 upstream Rust source files carry tests. They are the regression net for the modules this port
  claims not to touch.

## From agwinterm, the host terminal, whose plan is under triage alongside this one

- The control API is a versioned contract. `tests/conformance/control-api.json` is shared with a
  second product (agliteterm) and running in both repositories' CI, so a verb added there breaks a
  project that does not implement it.
- Never test against the real running instance or its data dir. A Debug build gets instance id
  `agwinterm-dev` with its own pipe and data dir; routing must be verified before results are
  trusted. Running against the real data dir has destroyed real user session state before.
- MSBuild silently serves stale DLLs in several documented ways. "It builds" is not evidence the
  new code ran.

## How this project is built

ralphex executes plans autonomously, task by task. revmux reviews every plan and every diff before
it is accepted. `.revmux/` is committed, so the review standard is versioned with the code.

A checked-in lens is executed by a headless agent with a shell. Treat `.revmux/` as code.

1	# winterm-browser — port brief
2	
3	A Windows-native port of [zenbu-labs/terminal-browser](https://github.com/zenbu-labs/terminal-browser):
4	a real Chromium browser rendered inside a terminal pane. The host terminal is
5	[agwinterm](file:///C:/Users/boris/source/agwinterm) (`TERM_PROGRAM=agwinterm`).
6	
7	Upstream sources are kept for reference (never committed) at `.reference/terminal-browser/`.
8	The agwinterm source tree lives at `C:\Users\boris\source\agwinterm`.
9	
10	## Why a port and not a build flag
11	
12	Upstream cannot run on Windows, for two *independent* reasons. Either alone is fatal.
13	
14	### Blocker 1 — the Rust engine does not compile on Windows
15	
16	`cargo check --workspace` in `.reference/terminal-browser/engine/` on `windows/amd64`,
17	Rust 1.93.1 (the pinned `rust-toolchain.toml` channel), fails with **41 errors** in `pixel-core`.
18	The unix assumptions are unconditional — not `cfg`-gated — so there is nothing to switch on:
19	
20	| upstream file | unix-only API |
21	|---|---|
22	| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:4` | `rustix::termios::{OptionalActions, Termios}` — raw mode via `tcgetattr`/`tcsetattr` |
23	| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:505,544` | `rustix::shm::unlink` |
24	| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:1161` | `OpenOptions::mode(0o600)` (unix-only trait) |
25	| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:770` | `rustix::pipe::pipe` + `fcntl_setfl(O_NONBLOCK)` |
26	| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/herdr.rs:2,308` | `std::os::unix::net::{UnixStream, UnixListener}` |
27	| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/ghostty.rs:121` | `rustix::process::kill_process(pid, Signal::USR2)` |
28	
29	`pixel-node` gates its zero-copy surface transports on `cfg(target_os="macos")` (IOSurface) and
30	`cfg(target_os="linux")` (shm). **There is no `cfg(windows)` anywhere in the workspace.**
31	The installer agrees: `scripts/install.sh:9-14` maps only `Darwin-arm64`, `Linux-x86_64`,
32	`Linux-aarch64`, and otherwise prints *"terminal-browser does not support …"*.
33	
34	### Blocker 2 — ConPTY strips the transport
35	
36	Upstream's entire output model is *write Kitty graphics APC escapes to stdout at frame rate*.
37	On Windows, ConPTY strips APC before the host emulator ever sees it. agwinterm's own gap
38	analysis states this (`docs/agterm-gap-analysis.md:41`):
39	
40	> Kitty graphics via the control pipe (docxy), delivered out-of-band because ConPTY strips APC.
41	
42	So even a hypothetical compiling `pixel-core` would paint a blank pane. The transport must change,
43	which is the real reason this is a port rather than a patch.
44	
45	## What agwinterm already gives us
46	
47	The host side is further along than the guest side, and this is what makes the port tractable:
48	
49	- **Kitty graphics model** — `Agwinterm.Core/KittyGraphics.cs` holds `KittyImage` (raw PNG or
50	  RGB/RGBA pixels) and `ImagePlacement` with `Cols`/`Rows` cell-span scaling (Kitty `c=`/`r=`),
51	  so one full-pane image scales to the grid. Parsing lives in
52	  `native/agwinterm-core/src/emulator.rs` (`finalize_kitty_image`, `parse_kitty_keys`).
53	- **An out-of-band frame path already exists** — `Agwinterm.Pty/ControlServer.cs:249`
54	  `image.frame` takes an `images[]` array, content-signature-caches each id to skip
55	  re-transmits, reads pixel bytes *off* the render lock, and swaps placements under a
56	  microsecond-scale lock. It is a video path fed by file paths.
57	- **Input is solved** — SGR mouse (`?1000/?1002/?1003/?1006`,
58	  `Agwinterm.Core/TerminalEmulator.cs:403-405`) and the kitty keyboard protocol
59	  (`emulator.rs:809 kitty_keyboard`). No macOS-style background helper app is needed;
60	  upstream's Swift input helper has no analogue here and is simply dropped.
61	
62	## Architecture
63	
64	An earlier draft of this brief proposed dropping `pixel-core` wholesale and letting agwinterm
65	composite. Measurement says otherwise, and the cheaper design won.
66	
67	### The unix dependency is concentrated, not pervasive
68	
69	Counting `rustix::` / `std::os::unix` / `termios` / `libc::` / `/dev/tty` references per module
70	across `pixel-core`'s 22 source files:
71	
72	| module | hits | disposition |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| `terminal.rs` | **64** | replace — this is the tty layer and the Kitty-to-stdout encoder |
75	| `herdr.rs` | 2 | port — `UnixStream`/`UnixListener` → Windows named pipes (or gate off for v1) |
76	| `ghostty.rs` | 2 | drop — ghostty-specific `SIGUSR2` signalling, no Windows analogue |
77	| **all 19 others** | **0** | **keep unchanged** |
78	
79	`canvas.rs`, `paint.rs`, `text_input.rs`, `image_cache.rs`, `menu.rs`, `kitty.rs`, `shape.rs`,
80	`wrap.rs`, `style.rs`, `scrollbar.rs` and the rest are already portable Rust — taffy, tiny-skia and
81	fontdue are all cross-platform. **The compositor and UI toolkit port for free.** This matters
82	because the browser chrome (tab strip, URL bar, menus, modals — `browser/src/ui/*.tsx`) renders
83	through `pixel-react` into `pixel-core`. Dropping `pixel-core` would have meant rewriting the entire
84	browser chrome; keeping it means the chrome is untouched.
85	
86	So the port is: **replace one module, port one, drop one, keep nineteen.**
87	
88	### No patched Electron needed
89	
90	Upstream's fast paths require an Electron fork they build themselves
91	(`scripts/fetch-electron.sh` pulls from `zenbu-labs/electron-releases`, macOS and Linux only) —
92	`useSharedTexture` on darwin, `useSharedMemory` on linux (`browser/src/page/offscreen.ts`).
93	
94	But `presentPaint` already falls through to `presentBitmap` (`browser/src/page/paint.ts:104`),
95	which uses stock Electron's `paint` event: `image.toBitmap()` →
96	`surface.present({ bgra, width, height, damage })`, coalesced by `BitmapPresenter`. That path
97	runs on **stock Electron on Windows with no patch**, and `Surface.present` is the exact seam the
98	Windows backend plugs into.
99	
100	Optimising past the bitmap copy is deliberately deferred. Stock Electron on Windows can expose a
101	D3D11 shared-texture handle, and agwinterm renders with Direct2D, so a genuine zero-copy path
102	exists later — it is not v1.
103	
104	| layer | upstream (macOS/Linux) | winterm-browser |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| Browser + chrome UI | Electron OSR + React via `pixel-react` | **unchanged** |
107	| Compositor / layout / text | `pixel-core` (taffy / tiny-skia / fontdue) | **unchanged** — already portable |
108	| Electron frame capture | patched Electron: IOSurface / shm | **stock Electron bitmap path** (already written) |
109	| Frame pixels → terminal | Kitty APC → stdout | Windows file-mapping shared BGRA ring → control pipe |
110	| tty layer (`terminal.rs`) | termios raw mode, `/dev/tty`, shm, kitty encoder | **rewritten** for Windows console + agwinterm |
111	| Raw-mode input | termios + macOS Swift helper | Windows console VT input; helper dropped entirely |
112	| `herdr.rs` IPC | `UnixStream` | Windows named pipes |
113	| `ghostty.rs` | `SIGUSR2` to ghostty | dropped |
114	| CLI / terminals / store | TypeScript | mostly portable; `ssh.ts` and `sandbox.ts` (apparmor) need Windows work |
115	
116	### Chosen transport
117	
118	Extend agwinterm with a shared-memory frame command so Electron's paint buffer reaches the
119	renderer with **no PNG encode, no disk round-trip and no base64**:
120	
121	```
122	Electron paint(BGRA)
123	  └─> CreateFileMapping (shared BGRA ring)
124	        └─> pipe: {"cmd":"image.frameshm","args":{"handle":..,"w":..,"h":..}}
125	              └─> KittyImage (f=32, raw RGBA)
126	                    └─> D2D texture
127	```
128	
129	This spans **two repositories**: agwinterm gains the command, winterm-browser produces the frames.
130	The existing file-based `image.frame` stays as the fallback and as the bring-up path.
131

# winterm-browser — port brief

A Windows-native port of [zenbu-labs/terminal-browser](https://github.com/zenbu-labs/terminal-browser):
a real Chromium browser rendered inside a terminal pane. The host terminal is
[agwinterm](file:///C:/Users/boris/source/agwinterm) (`TERM_PROGRAM=agwinterm`).

Upstream sources are kept for reference (never committed) at `.reference/terminal-browser/`.
The agwinterm source tree lives at `C:\Users\boris\source\agwinterm`.

## Why a port and not a build flag

Upstream cannot run on Windows, for two *independent* reasons. Either alone is fatal.

### Blocker 1 — the Rust engine does not compile on Windows

`cargo check --workspace` in `.reference/terminal-browser/engine/` on `windows/amd64`,
Rust 1.93.1 (the pinned `rust-toolchain.toml` channel), fails with **41 errors** in `pixel-core`.
The unix assumptions are unconditional — not `cfg`-gated — so there is nothing to switch on:

| upstream file | unix-only API |
|---|---|
| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:4` | `rustix::termios::{OptionalActions, Termios}` — raw mode via `tcgetattr`/`tcsetattr` |
| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:505,544` | `rustix::shm::unlink` |
| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:1161` | `OpenOptions::mode(0o600)` (unix-only trait) |
| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs:770` | `rustix::pipe::pipe` + `fcntl_setfl(O_NONBLOCK)` |
| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/herdr.rs:2,308` | `std::os::unix::net::{UnixStream, UnixListener}` |
| `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/ghostty.rs:121` | `rustix::process::kill_process(pid, Signal::USR2)` |

`pixel-node` gates its zero-copy surface transports on `cfg(target_os="macos")` (IOSurface) and
`cfg(target_os="linux")` (shm). **There is no `cfg(windows)` anywhere in the workspace.**
The installer agrees: `scripts/install.sh:9-14` maps only `Darwin-arm64`, `Linux-x86_64`,
`Linux-aarch64`, and otherwise prints *"terminal-browser does not support …"*.

### Blocker 2 — ConPTY strips the transport

Upstream's entire output model is *write Kitty graphics APC escapes to stdout at frame rate*.
On Windows, ConPTY strips APC before the host emulator ever sees it. agwinterm's own gap
analysis states this (`docs/agterm-gap-analysis.md:41`):

> Kitty graphics via the control pipe (docxy), delivered out-of-band because ConPTY strips APC.

So even a hypothetical compiling `pixel-core` would paint a blank pane. The transport must change,
which is the real reason this is a port rather than a patch.

## What agwinterm already gives us

The host side is further along than the guest side, and this is what makes the port tractable:

- **Kitty graphics model** — `Agwinterm.Core/KittyGraphics.cs` holds `KittyImage` (raw PNG or
  RGB/RGBA pixels) and `ImagePlacement` with `Cols`/`Rows` cell-span scaling (Kitty `c=`/`r=`),
  so one full-pane image scales to the grid. Parsing lives in
  `native/agwinterm-core/src/emulator.rs` (`finalize_kitty_image`, `parse_kitty_keys`).
- **An out-of-band frame path already exists** — `Agwinterm.Pty/ControlServer.cs:249`
  `image.frame` takes an `images[]` array, content-signature-caches each id to skip
  re-transmits, reads pixel bytes *off* the render lock, and swaps placements under a
  microsecond-scale lock. It is a video path fed by file paths.
- **Input is solved** — SGR mouse (`?1000/?1002/?1003/?1006`,
  `Agwinterm.Core/TerminalEmulator.cs:403-405`) and the kitty keyboard protocol
  (`emulator.rs:809 kitty_keyboard`). No macOS-style background helper app is needed;
  upstream's Swift input helper has no analogue here and is simply dropped.

## Architecture

An earlier draft of this brief proposed dropping `pixel-core` wholesale and letting agwinterm
composite. Measurement says otherwise, and the cheaper design won.

### The unix dependency is concentrated, not pervasive

Counting `rustix::` / `std::os::unix` / `termios` / `libc::` / `/dev/tty` references per module
across `pixel-core`'s 22 source files:

| module | hits | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.rs` | **64** | replace — this is the tty layer and the Kitty-to-stdout encoder |
| `herdr.rs` | 2 | port — `UnixStream`/`UnixListener` → Windows named pipes (or gate off for v1) |
| `ghostty.rs` | 2 | drop — ghostty-specific `SIGUSR2` signalling, no Windows analogue |
| **all 19 others** | **0** | **keep unchanged** |

`canvas.rs`, `paint.rs`, `text_input.rs`, `image_cache.rs`, `menu.rs`, `kitty.rs`, `shape.rs`,
`wrap.rs`, `style.rs`, `scrollbar.rs` and the rest are already portable Rust — taffy, tiny-skia and
fontdue are all cross-platform. **The compositor and UI toolkit port for free.** This matters
because the browser chrome (tab strip, URL bar, menus, modals — `browser/src/ui/*.tsx`) renders
through `pixel-react` into `pixel-core`. Dropping `pixel-core` would have meant rewriting the entire
browser chrome; keeping it means the chrome is untouched.

So the port is: **replace one module, port one, drop one, keep nineteen.**

### No patched Electron needed

Upstream's fast paths require an Electron fork they build themselves
(`scripts/fetch-electron.sh` pulls from `zenbu-labs/electron-releases`, macOS and Linux only) —
`useSharedTexture` on darwin, `useSharedMemory` on linux (`browser/src/page/offscreen.ts`).

But `presentPaint` already falls through to `presentBitmap` (`browser/src/page/paint.ts:104`),
which uses stock Electron's `paint` event: `image.toBitmap()` →
`surface.present({ bgra, width, height, damage })`, coalesced by `BitmapPresenter`. That path
runs on **stock Electron on Windows with no patch**, and `Surface.present` is the exact seam the
Windows backend plugs into.

Optimising past the bitmap copy is deliberately deferred. Stock Electron on Windows can expose a
D3D11 shared-texture handle, and agwinterm renders with Direct2D, so a genuine zero-copy path
exists later — it is not v1.

| layer | upstream (macOS/Linux) | winterm-browser |
|---|---|---|
| Browser + chrome UI | Electron OSR + React via `pixel-react` | **unchanged** |
| Compositor / layout / text | `pixel-core` (taffy / tiny-skia / fontdue) | **unchanged** — already portable |
| Electron frame capture | patched Electron: IOSurface / shm | **stock Electron bitmap path** (already written) |
| Frame pixels → terminal | Kitty APC → stdout | Windows file-mapping shared BGRA ring → control pipe |
| tty layer (`terminal.rs`) | termios raw mode, `/dev/tty`, shm, kitty encoder | **rewritten** for Windows console + agwinterm |
| Raw-mode input | termios + macOS Swift helper | Windows console VT input; helper dropped entirely |
| `herdr.rs` IPC | `UnixStream` | Windows named pipes |
| `ghostty.rs` | `SIGUSR2` to ghostty | dropped |
| CLI / terminals / store | TypeScript | mostly portable; `ssh.ts` and `sandbox.ts` (apparmor) need Windows work |

### Chosen transport

Extend agwinterm with a shared-memory frame command so Electron's paint buffer reaches the
renderer with **no PNG encode, no disk round-trip and no base64**:

```
Electron paint(BGRA)
  └─> CreateFileMapping (shared BGRA ring)
        └─> pipe: {"cmd":"image.frameshm","args":{"handle":..,"w":..,"h":..}}
              └─> KittyImage (f=32, raw RGBA)
                    └─> D2D texture
```

This spans **two repositories**: agwinterm gains the command, winterm-browser produces the frames.
The existing file-based `image.frame` stays as the fallback and as the bring-up path.

## Working agreement

- **ralphex** is the implementer. Plans live in `docs/plans/`; execution is autonomous.
- **revmux** is the review harness, run natively on Windows. Every plan and every diff goes
  through it before it is accepted. `.revmux/` is committed, so the review standard is versioned
  with the code.
- Both `claude` and `codex` CLIs are present, so full-roster profiles (`comprehensive`,
  `grill-me`) are available rather than `claude-only`.

## Verified environment

Established by direct check on this machine, 2026-08-21:

| tool | state |
|---|---|
| Windows | 11 Home Single Language, 10.0.26200 |
| agwinterm | 0.17.2, `AGWINTERM_ENABLED=1` |
| Go | 1.26.1 windows/amd64 |
| Rust | cargo 1.96.0 |
| Node | v22.19.0 |
| Python | 3.13.7 |
| revmux | builds and runs natively on Windows (`lock_windows.go`, `procgroup_windows.go`); both `--task` and `/task:` flag styles accepted |
| ralphex | installed at `~/go/bin/ralphex.exe` |
| claude / codex | both on PATH |
| WSL | **not installed — and explicitly out of scope.** This is a Windows-native port. |

# winterm-browser — Windows-native port

## Overview

Bring terminal-browser to Windows, hosted by agwinterm: a real Chromium browser rendered inside a
terminal pane, with working keyboard and mouse, on stock Electron, with no WSL.

The authoritative design is [`docs/design/00-port-brief.md`](../design/00-port-brief.md). Read it
first — it records what was measured rather than assumed, and it already overturned one plausible
architecture. In short:

- Upstream cannot run here for two independent reasons: `pixel-core` does not compile on Windows
  (41 errors), and its transport — Kitty APC escapes on stdout — is stripped by ConPTY before any
  Windows emulator sees it.
- But the unix dependency is **concentrated, not pervasive**: 64 of 68 unix-API references live in
  `terminal.rs`, and **19 of 22 `pixel-core` modules have none at all**. The compositor, layout and
  text stack (taffy, tiny-skia, fontdue) are portable Rust. That matters because the browser chrome
  renders through `pixel-react` into `pixel-core` — dropping it would have meant rewriting the whole
  chrome.
- Upstream's fast frame paths need an Electron fork they build themselves, macOS and Linux only. But
  `presentBitmap` (`browser/src/page/paint.ts:104`) already implements a stock-Electron path:
  `image.toBitmap()` → `surface.present({bgra, width, height, damage})`. Windows gets that for free.

**So the port is: replace one module, port one, drop one, keep nineteen** — plus a new output
backend that speaks agwinterm's control pipe instead of writing escapes to a tty.

## Context (from discovery)

Upstream reference (read-only, never committed): `.reference/terminal-browser/`.
agwinterm source: `C:\Users\boris\source\agwinterm`.

| area | file | note |
|---|---|---|
| tty layer to replace | `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/terminal.rs` | 64 unix hits: termios raw mode, `/dev/tty`, `rustix::shm`, `pipe`+`O_NONBLOCK`, and the Kitty-to-stdout encoder |
| IPC to port | `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/herdr.rs` | `UnixStream`/`UnixListener` → named pipes, or gated off for v1 |
| to drop | `engine/crates/pixel-core/src/ghostty.rs` | `SIGUSR2` to ghostty; no Windows analogue |
| keep unchanged | the other 19 `pixel-core` modules | `canvas`, `paint`, `text_input`, `image_cache`, `menu`, `kitty`, `shape`, `wrap`, `style`, `scrollbar`, … |
| napi bridge | `engine/crates/pixel-node/src/{lib,surface}.rs` | `SurfacePixels` gates IOSurface on macOS and shm on linux; the `Owned { bgra, width, height }` variant is the Windows path and already exists |
| the seam | `Surface.present` from `pixel-react` | what `browser/` calls; the Windows backend plugs in here |
| Electron capture | `browser/src/page/{offscreen,paint}.ts` | `offscreenPreferences` branches darwin/linux; `initOffscreenMode` throws on darwin without shared textures |
| host frame path | agwinterm `src/Agwinterm.Pty/ControlServer.cs:249` | `image.frame` today; `image.frameshm` per the agwinterm plan |
| host input | agwinterm `TerminalEmulator.cs:403-405`, `emulator.rs:809` | SGR mouse `?1000/?1002/?1003/?1006` and kitty keyboard already work |

**Tooling upstream already uses**, and this port keeps: `cargo nextest run --workspace`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and
`node --test` for the TypeScript packages. 37 Rust source files carry tests; they are the
regression net for everything in the "keep unchanged" column.

## Constraints

- **Windows-native only. WSL is out of scope** and is not an acceptable fallback for any task.
- **Stock Electron.** Do not fetch or build a patched Electron; if a task seems to need one, the
  task is wrong. `scripts/fetch-electron.sh` is upstream's, and it does not apply here.
- **This plan depends on the agwinterm plan** for the shm fast path only
  (`agwinterm/docs/plans/20260821-image-frameshm-command.md`, contract in
  `agwinterm/docs/specs/image-frameshm.md`). Everything up to and including the
  first-frame-on-screen milestone uses the file-based `image.frame`, which needs no agwinterm change.
  If the contract is not ready when Task 9 starts, stop and say so rather than inventing a shape.
- **Never test against the real agwinterm instance.** Use a Debug agwinterm (instance id
  `agwinterm-dev`, its own pipe and data dir) and verify routing with
  `agwintermctl --pipe agwinterm-dev tree` before trusting any result. Running against the real
  data dir has destroyed real session state before.
- **Do not weaken the "keep unchanged" 19 modules to make something compile.** If one of them needs
  a change, that is a finding worth recording in the plan (➕), not a quiet edit.
- Upstream's licence and provenance travel with the vendored code.

## Development Approach

- **Testing approach**: Regular (code first, then tests).
- Complete each task fully before moving to the next.
- Make small, focused changes.
- **CRITICAL: every task MUST include new/updated tests** for code changes in that task.
  - unit tests for new and modified functions, as separate checklist items
  - success and error scenarios both
- **CRITICAL: all tests must pass before starting the next task.**
- **CRITICAL: update this plan file when scope changes during implementation.**
- Run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` as part of "tests pass".

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit tests**: required every task. Rust via `cargo nextest`, TypeScript via `node --test`.
- **Platform-behaviour tests**: the console and control-pipe layers are where assumptions die.
  Prefer a test that drives the real thing (a real named pipe, a real `MemoryMappedFile`, a real
  Debug agwinterm) over a mock that encodes a guess about Win32.
- **Visual confirmation** is a milestone, not a test: Task 8 is "a page is legibly on screen".
  Screenshot verification belongs in Post-Completion, not in a checkbox.
- **No e2e browser-automation suite in this plan.** Scope is a working port.

## Progress Tracking

- Mark completed items with `[x]` immediately when done.
- Add newly discovered tasks with ➕ prefix.
- Document issues/blockers with ⚠️ prefix.
- Update the plan when implementation deviates from scope.

- [ ] reuse ids across frames so agwinterm's content-signature cache behaves as designed
- [ ] clean up temp files, and survive a frame whose file write fails
- [ ] keep this path permanently as the fallback and as the thing the shm path is diffed against —

1	# Shared-memory frame command (`image.frameshm`)
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Add a control-pipe command that accepts browser-rate BGRA frames through a shared memory mapping
6	instead of through files, so a producer can drive a pane at video rates without a PNG encode or a
7	disk round-trip on every frame.
8	
9	The consumer is [winterm-browser](file:///C:/Users/boris/source/winterm-browser), a Windows-native
10	port of terminal-browser that renders Chromium into an agwinterm pane. Its design brief is
11	`C:\Users\boris\source\winterm-browser\docs\design\00-port-brief.md`. That project is blocked on
12	this command, and this plan defines the contract it codes against — so the wire shape here is the
13	deliverable, not just the implementation.
14	
15	**Problem it solves.** `image.frame` (`ControlServer.cs:249`) is already a frame path: it takes an
16	`images[]` array, content-signature-caches each id to skip re-transmits, reads pixel bytes off the
17	render lock, and swaps placements under a microsecond-scale lock. But every image arrives as a
18	`path`, so a 30fps full-pane producer must PNG-encode and write a file 30 times a second and
19	agwinterm must read it back. For a document viewer like docxy that is fine. For a browser it is not.
20	
21	**Why this is worth doing beyond the browser.** The expensive part of `image.frame` is not the
22	placement machinery, which is already good — it is the format and the transport. Anything that
23	generates pixels rather than loading them (a video preview, a plot that animates, a remote frame
24	buffer) hits the same wall.
25	
26	## Context (from discovery)
27	
28	- `src/Agwinterm.Pty/ControlServer.cs:249` — `image.frame` dispatch; `HandleImageFrame` at ~line 425
29	  is the model to follow: phase 1 resolves placements and owns pixel bytes **off** the render lock,
30	  phase 2 takes a brief lock for dictionary/list swaps only.
31	- `src/Agwinterm.Core/KittyGraphics.cs` — `KittyFormat { Rgb = 24, Rgba = 32, Png = 100 }`,
32	  `KittyImage(Id, Format, Width, Height, Data)`, `ImagePlacement(ImageId, Row, Col, Cols, Rows,
33	  SrcX, SrcY, SrcW, SrcH)`.
34	- `src/Agwinterm.Pty/ISession.cs:64,66` — `Inject(ReadOnlySpan<byte>)` and
35	  `MutateLocked(Action<ITerminalCore>)`; both take the render lock internally.
36	- `tests/Agwinterm.Pty.Tests/ControlServerTests.cs` and `ControlApiTests.cs` — where control-verb
37	  tests live.
38	- `tests/conformance/control-api.json` — **shared with agliteterm**; the same spec runs in both
39	  repositories' CI. See the constraint below.
40	
41	## Constraints
42	
43	- **Do not add `image.frameshm` to `tests/conformance/control-api.json`.** That file is a contract
44	  agliteterm must also satisfy, and adding a verb there fails agliteterm's build for a command it
45	  does not implement. Test this verb in agwinterm's own xunit suites only. If it should later become
46	  part of the shared dialect, that is a separate decision made with agliteterm in hand.
47	- **Frames must never tear.** A producer writing while the renderer reads is the default failure
48	  mode of any shared buffer; the design must make a torn read impossible, not unlikely.
49	- **A dead or lying producer must not take the terminal down.** The name, dimensions, stride and
50	  offsets all arrive from another process and every one of them is untrusted input into a pointer
51	  computation. Validate against the actual mapped view length before any copy.
52	- **`ControlServer` int args must be JSON numbers, not strings** — `GetInt` throws
53	  `"requires an element of type 'Number'"` otherwise. The ctl serializes `cargs` by type, so parse
54	  with `int.TryParse` on the CLI side.
55	- Backward compatibility: `image.frame` keeps working unchanged. This is an additional verb.
56	- Build discipline (these have cost hours before): close the running dev instance before building;
57	  build `src/Agwinterm.Win32` **explicitly** so its copy of `Agwinterm.Pty.dll` is not stale;
58	  a plain solution build outputs to a *different* directory than a project build.
59	- Test against an isolated instance: a Debug build auto-uses instance id `agwinterm-dev` with its own
60	  data dir and pipe. Drive it with `agwintermctl --pipe agwinterm-dev`. **Never** run against the
61	  real `agwinterm` pipe or data dir.
62	
63	## Development Approach
64	
65	- **Testing approach**: Regular (code first, then tests).
66	- Complete each task fully before moving to the next.

# Shared-memory frame command (`image.frameshm`)

## Overview

Add a control-pipe command that accepts browser-rate BGRA frames through a shared memory mapping
instead of through files, so a producer can drive a pane at video rates without a PNG encode or a
disk round-trip on every frame.

The consumer is [winterm-browser](file:///C:/Users/boris/source/winterm-browser), a Windows-native
port of terminal-browser that renders Chromium into an agwinterm pane. Its design brief is
`C:\Users\boris\source\winterm-browser\docs\design\00-port-brief.md`. That project is blocked on
this command, and this plan defines the contract it codes against — so the wire shape here is the
deliverable, not just the implementation.

**Problem it solves.** `image.frame` (`ControlServer.cs:249`) is already a frame path: it takes an

render lock, and swaps placements under a microsecond-scale lock. But every image arrives as a
`path`, so a 30fps full-pane producer must PNG-encode and write a file 30 times a second and
agwinterm must read it back. For a document viewer like docxy that is fine. For a browser it is not.

placement machinery, which is already good — it is the format and the transport. Anything that
generates pixels rather than loading them (a video preview, a plot that animates, a remote frame
buffer) hits the same wall.

  repositories' CI. See the constraint below.

First boot of a single pwsh pane already logged these — prioritized checklist below, with ConPTY-masking notes (many classic queries never reach us because conhost answers them itself; what shows up in our log is genuinely OUR job).

## Observed in the log (real, forwarded to us by ConPTY)

- [ ] **`?1004` focus reporting** — requested by *every* shell at startup. When on, the terminal must send `ESC[I` (focus in) / `ESC[O` (focus out) on `WM_SETFOCUS`/`WM_KILLFOCUS` **and on pane switch** (agwinterm's per-pane focus matters, not just window focus). - [ ] **`?9001` win32-input-mode** — ConPTY asks us for Windows Terminal's enhanced key encoding. Honoring it (encode keys as win32-input-mode records when on) improves key fidelity through conhost. Evidence: `MODE ?9001 h` on every session.
- [ ] **`?2026` synchronized output** — TUIs batch frames between begin/end to eliminate flicker/tearing; the terminal should defer repaints while a batch is open (with a timeout guard). Evidence: `MODE ?2026 h`.
- [ ] **DECSCUSR (`CSI Ps SP q`)** — per-app cursor shape (bar/underline/block, blink). We render one configured style; apps that set it get ignored. Evidence: `CSI 3 q`.
- [ ] **BEL (0x07)** — no bell at all: no sound, no visual flash, no badge. Could map to the existing status/notification machinery. Evidence: `C0 0x07`.

- DSR/CPR (`CSI 6n`), DA1/DA2 (`CSI c`, `CSI >c`) — conhost responds on our behalf; only relevant for the defterm-handoff/attach path.

findings.title: agwinterm never encodes kitty keyboard on the input side — "agwinterm emits both" is false for keyboard
findings.body:
Task 3 states "decode SGR mouse reports (?1006) and kitty keyboard sequences — agwinterm emits both, so the work is consuming them, not negotiating them", and the brief (docs/design/00-port-brief.md:57-60) generalises this to "Input is solved". I traced the host side and the keyboard half does not exist.

Established by reading: agwinterm's only key encoder is `OnKeyDown` at C:/Users/boris/source/agwinterm/src/Agwinterm.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:636-695. It is a legacy VT table — `\x1b[1;<mod>A` for arrows, `\x1bOP` for F1, `\r`, `\x7f`. It never reads `KeyboardFlags` (exposed at Agwinterm.Core/ITerminalCore.cs:38) and emits no CSI-u form anywhere; I grepped `src` and `native` for a CSI-u/key-encode path and found none. `kitty_keyboard` (native/agwinterm-core/src/emulator.rs:805-815) and `keyboard_flags()` (:293) only parse the client's DECSET and answer its query — agwinterm acknowledges the protocol it does not speak. Concretely: no key-release events, no event-type field, no repeat distinction; `Ctrl+A..Z` collapses to a control byte at MainWindow.xaml.cs:651-657 so Ctrl+Shift+X is indistinguishable from Ctrl+X; and Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+T/N/W are intercepted for agwinterm's own UI at :643-646 and never reach the client at all — Ctrl+Shift+T is the browser's reopen-closed-tab.

What follows from that (my inference): Task 9 is under-scoped by a feature that lives in the *other* repository, and this is a second cross-repo dependency that the plan does not record. Constraint line 54-58 pins only the frameshm contract.

The project's own record agrees, in your words. agwinterm's docs/windows-terminal-gap-analysis.md:61 lists "win32-input-mode / Kitty keyboard protocol | CSI ? 9001 h | **Missing** | M". Issue yeroo/agwinterm#98 ("VT protocol audit", your own, closed) has an unchecked box reading "`?9001` win32-input-mode — ConPTY asks us for Windows Terminal's enhanced key encoding. Honoring it (**encode keys as win32-input-mode records when on**) improves key fidelity through conhost." That issue also shows the same parse-but-don't-emit pattern for `?1004` focus reporting, so this is a documented class rather than one oversight. On the close: #98 has zero comments and was closed within nine seconds of #105 and #91, so it is a bulk close carrying no reasoning — it records that the gap was scoped, not that it was declined.

One thing would overturn this: if legacy VT keys are good enough for the browsing you actually intend, key-up and Ctrl+Shift being unavailable is a quality ceiling rather than a blocker, and Task 9 stands as written.
findings.fix: Either add a task (here or in agwinterm) to implement host-side key encoding — kitty CSI-u or win32-input-mode per #98 — and record it as the second pinned cross-repo dependency alongside frameshm; or restate Task 3/Task 9 and the brief's "Input is solved" to say keyboard is legacy-VT fidelity only, and state what that costs.

findings.title: Nothing in the 13 tasks installs or launches Electron on Windows; Task 8 is blocked from both ends
findings.body:
Goal item 3 asks whether the Task 8 milestone is reachable where it sits. It is not, for two reasons that both sit outside Task 8.

**Task 1 aborts.** browser/package.json:7 is `"postinstall": "bash ../scripts/fetch-electron.sh"`. Task 1 (docs/plans/20260821-windows-port.md:102-103) explicitly does *not* copy `scripts/`, naming `fetch-electron.sh`. So the postinstall points at a file that will not exist. Even if it were copied, scripts/fetch-electron.sh:8-13 is a `uname` case that ends `*) echo "fetch-electron: unsupported platform"; exit 1`. Either way `pnpm install` — Task 1's own checklist item at :106 — fails on the browser package rather than producing the "which packages install cleanly" record it asks for. No task in the plan removes or replaces that postinstall.

**Task 8's launcher is deferred to Task 11.** cli/src/main.ts is what spawns Electron (browser/package.json:10 `"start": "... exec node ../cli/dist/main.js"`). `electronBinary()` at cli/src/main.ts:74-78 resolves `browser/node_modules/electron/dist/` + `ELECTRON_DEV_BIN`, which is `["electron"]` on every non-darwin platform (:65-68). On Windows that file is `electron.exe`, so `browserLaunchCommand`'s `fs.existsSync` guard at :80-86 fails and reports `missing … — build the browser first`, which is the wrong diagnosis. cli/src/main.ts is Task 11 (:241-252), three tasks after Task 8 (:198-210).

Worth stating because it cuts the other way: `"electron": "43.3.0"` is a plain devDependency at browser/package.json:22. So stock Electron for Windows does arrive through an ordinary install once the postinstall is neutralised — the no-patched-Electron premise is better grounded than the brief argues, and the missing piece is plumbing, not architecture.

Established by reading; I did not run `pnpm install` (this review is read-only) and node_modules is not present, so the `.exe` suffix is from the electron package's standard Windows layout rather than from disk. Two things would overturn it: pnpm being configured to skip the workspace project's own postinstall, or Task 8 being understood as licence to improvise a launcher rather than use the CLI.
findings.fix: Add to Task 1: drop or Windows-guard browser/package.json's postinstall so `pnpm install` completes on stock Electron. Move the `electronBinary()`/`ELECTRON_DEV_BIN` `.exe` fix out of Task 11 into a task before Task 8, or state in Task 8 that it launches Electron directly and defers the CLI.

Task 2 says "move the existing unix implementation behind `#[cfg(unix)]`" (:120-121) and names its real deliverable as "`cargo check --workspace` is clean on Windows" (:126). Those two bullets are in tension, because terminal.rs is not only a tty layer.

Established by reading: terminal.rs is 2617 lines and defines the crate's whole input vocabulary in the same file as the termios/shm/pipe code — `Event` (:11), `KeyEvent` (:26), `KeyKind` (:49), `Mods` (:57), `Key` (:65), `Mouse` (:94), `MouseKind` (:103), `MouseButton` (:114), `TerminalColors` (:122), `ColorSlot` (:139), `WindowSize` (:175), `Terminal` (:227), `Waker` (:304), `SessionEnv` (:315). Twelve other files import `crate::terminal::*`, and they are in the keep-unchanged column: engine/keys.rs (`KeyEvent`, `KeyKind`, and ~30 `Key::` arms), engine/doc.rs, engine/input.rs (`Mouse`), engine/embed.rs (`Mouse`, `MouseKind`), engine/clipboard.rs (`Terminal`), native.rs (`Waker`).

The alternative — lifting the types into a portable module — means editing the `use` lines in those twelve files, which collides with the constraint at :63-64 ("Do not weaken the 19 keep-unchanged modules") and would be flagged by Task 12's `git diff` check at :260-261.

There is a clean route the plan does not name: keep terminal.rs present on Windows as a facade that `pub use`s the portable types and gates only the impl. An executor following the bullet literally will not find it before breaking twelve modules.

Overturned if ralphex is expected to redesign around checklist bullets rather than follow them.

Say so in the bullet, and note in Task 12 that a re-export shim is the expected diff.

findings.title: The brief and the agwinterm plan disagree on the shm wire shape — `handle` versus a named mapping
findings.body:
Goal item 4 asks whether the contract between the two repos is actually pinned. On the one field that crosses the process boundary, the two documents say different things.

The brief — which scope.md:7 calls "the authoritative design" and the plan at :8-9 says to read first — shows `{"cmd":"image.frameshm","args":{"handle":..,"w":..,"h":..}}`. The agwinterm plan defines the args as `{"images":[{"id","name":"Local\\...","slot","seq","width","height","stride","format","row","col","cols","rows"}]}` (context/agwinterm-dependency-plan.md:103-105) and opens the mapping with `MemoryMappedFile.OpenExisting(name, MemoryMappedFileRights.Read)` (:126).

These are not two spellings of one design. A Win32 HANDLE is process-local; its numeric value means nothing in the consumer unless the producer calls `DuplicateHandle` into the consumer's process, which requires knowing the consumer's PID and holding rights to it. The named-mapping shape is the workable one — so the brief is the wrong document here, and it is the document the plan tells the executor to trust. The Windows plan's own Task 10 (:229-232) says "create the named mapping", so the plan is right and the brief is stale; a reader who follows the plan's instruction to read the brief first gets the wrong shape.

A second gap in the same area, less certain: agwinterm's reader will "restrict accepted names to a fixed prefix in the `Local\` namespace" (dependency plan :130-131). The Windows plan's Task 10 never mentions a required prefix. If the exact prefix is not written into docs/specs/image-frameshm.md at agwinterm Task 1, the producer picks a name and is rejected at runtime with a validation error that looks like a bug.

Established by reading both documents; the DuplicateHandle point is Win32 semantics, not something I tested. Overturned if `handle` in the brief was always shorthand for the mapping name — in which case the fix is a word, but the word matters because ralphex codes against it.
findings.fix: Correct the brief's diagram to the named-mapping args before Task 10 starts rather than at Task 13, and add the exact `Local\` name prefix to the agwinterm Task 1 spec bullet so both sides pin the same string.

findings.title: Two slots plus an unsynchronised copying consumer does not make a torn read impossible
findings.body:
The dependency plan sets itself a hard constraint at :48-50: "Frames must never tear. A producer writing while the renderer reads is the default failure mode of any shared buffer; the design must make a torn read impossible, not unlikely." Its Technical Details at :198-203 then claims the two-slot scheme achieves that: "A frame in flight is therefore never the frame being read."

That claim does not hold for two slots without a back-channel. The consumer copies from the slot named by `ready`; nothing tells the producer when that copy finishes. Trace it: consumer reads `ready`=5 (slot A) and begins its memcpy. Producer fills slot B, publishes `ready`=6. Producer — free-running at browser paint rate, which is the entire premise — now needs a slot for its next frame, and the only other slot is A. It fills A while the consumer is still copying A. Torn read. A 1920x1080 BGRA frame is ~8 MB per copy, so the window is not narrow, and the failure gets *more* likely exactly when the producer is fast, which is the case the command exists for.

This is analysis of a written protocol, not of code — none exists yet — which is why my confidence is not higher. But the header already carries a slot count (:100-102), so the fix is cheap: three or more slots, or a consumer-written "currently reading" index the producer skips. It has to land in agwinterm Task 1, because the Windows plan's Task 10 (docs/plans/20260821-windows-port.md:229-231, "write BGRA into the inactive slot") codes against whatever that spec says, and "the inactive slot" is only well-defined if there is exactly one.

Overturned if the producer is to block until the consumer acknowledges, or is rate-limited below consumer speed by construction — neither is stated anywhere in either plan.
findings.fix: In agwinterm Task 1, either raise the slot count to three or add a consumer-published `reading` index to the header, and correct the Technical Details paragraph so the stated invariant matches the mechanism.

findings.title: Nothing sources the cell metrics and pane pixel size that Tasks 5, 8 and 9 all require
findings.body:
Task 5 requires "cell-span computation from pixel size and cell metrics" (:169-170), Task 9 requires a translation that "accounts for deviceScaleFactor and the pane's cell metrics" (:217-218), and Task 8 must render Chromium at some pixel size. I looked for where those numbers come from on Windows and found no supported source.

Established by reading: agwinterm's session-targeted control dispatch is `session.write/type/text/status` and `image.show/sixel/clear/frame` (ControlServer.cs:242-249). Grepping ControlServer.cs for `cell_width`/`cellW`/`CellSize`/`PixelWidth` returns nothing; `_cellW`/`_cellH` live only in Agwinterm.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:700 and are not exposed through the pipe. Grepping all of `src` and `native` for XTWINOPS (`14t`/`16t`/`18t`) returns nothing, so the client cannot ask the terminal for its pixel size either. Task 3's resize source (:139, console screen buffer info) yields cols and rows in character cells only.

The project's own record makes the query route worse, not better: issue yeroo/agwinterm#98 records, from a live VT tap, that "DSR/CPR (`CSI 6n`), DA1/DA2 — conhost responds on our behalf", and that an OSC 8 sent from a pane never reached the emulator. So a `CSI 14t` from inside a pane is likely to be answered by conhost or swallowed, never reaching agwinterm.

A workaround exists and the brief half-implies it: `image.frame` takes `cols`/`rows` (ControlServer.cs:444-445) and agwinterm scales the image to that cell span, so the producer can render at any resolution and let the terminal resample. But that costs text sharpness on a browser, and it is not what the plan says it will do. Either way this is potentially a third thing agwinterm must expose, alongside frameshm and key encoding.

Overturned if you intend to hardcode or configure cell metrics for v1, which would be reasonable — but the plan should say so, because an autonomous executor will otherwise go looking for a query that does not exist.
findings.fix: Decide and record where cell metrics come from — a new control verb, a config value, or "render at fixed resolution and let cols/rows scale it" — and add it to Task 4's client surface before Task 5 needs it.

findings.title: Mouse position is quantised to one character cell; there is no pixel-resolution mouse anywhere
findings.body:
Task 9 warns that "an off-by-one cell is a wrong click target", which frames the risk as translation accuracy. The real constraint is coarser: correct translation still lands the pointer on a lattice.

Established by reading: `SendMouse` at C:/Users/boris/source/agwinterm/src/Agwinterm.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:710-720 takes `(col,row)` from `CellAt` (:700), which is integer division of the pointer position by `_cellW`/`_cellH`, and emits `\x1b[<btn;col+1;row+1M`. Sub-cell position is discarded before the sequence is built, so it is not recoverable downstream by any amount of care in the port. `?1016` (SGR-Pixels) appears nowhere in agwinterm's `src` or `native` — I grepped for it and got nothing — and the emulator's mode handler covers only 1000/1002/1003/1006 (TerminalEmulator.cs:402-405). The brief's own quoted herdr metrics put a cell at 9x19 px.

What follows (my inference): in Chromium, every click, hover and drag snaps to a ~9x19 px grid. Hovering a 12 px link, placing a text caret mid-word, dragging a scrollbar or a column divider all become imprecise in a way no code in this repo can fix. That is a fair amount of "a real Chromium browser" (Overview, :5-6).

This is separate from the keyboard finding above and has a separate fix, which is why it is listed on its own. Overturned if cell-granularity pointing is acceptable for the intended use — plausible for reading and navigating, less so for the "page with a text input" and "heavy page" cases in Post-Completion (:294).
findings.fix: Either accept and record cell-granularity pointing as a known limitation in the brief and Task 9, or add `?1016` SGR-Pixels to agwinterm and to the pinned cross-repo dependency list.

Goal item 1 asks whether the unix-reference count is a failing proxy, and names arboard and fontdue. I checked. The count itself is sound; the proxy does fail, in a specific and narrow way.

Twelve other files import `crate::terminal::*`, and they are in the keep-unchanged column: engine/keys.rs (`KeyEvent`, `KeyKind`, and ~30 `Key::` arms), engine/doc.rs, engine/input.rs (`Mouse`), engine/embed.rs (`Mouse`, `MouseKind`), engine/clipboard.rs (`Terminal`), native.rs (`Waker`).

What follows (my inference, from Rust semantics): `#[cfg(unix)]` on the module removes those types on Windows and all twelve fail to compile, so the task's deliverable is unreachable by its own recipe. The alternative — lifting the types into a portable module — means editing the `use` lines in those twelve files, which collides with the constraint at :63-64 ("Do not weaken the 19 keep-unchanged modules") and would be flagged by Task 12's `git diff` check at :260-261.

There is a clean route the plan does not name: keep terminal.rs present on Windows as a facade that `pub use`s the portable types and gates only the impl. An executor following the bullet literally will not find it before breaking twelve modules.

Overturned if ralphex is expected to redesign around checklist bullets rather than follow them.
findings.fix: Split Task 2 explicitly: first extract the portable types (Event/Key/KeyEvent/Mods/Mouse/WindowSize/Waker/SessionEnv) into their own module and re-export from `terminal` so the 12 importers are untouched; only then cfg-gate the unix impl. Say so in the bullet, and note in Task 12 that a re-export shim is the expected diff.

findings.title: The brief and the agwinterm plan disagree on the shm wire shape — `handle` versus a named mapping
findings.body:
Goal item 4 asks whether the contract between the two repos is actually pinned. On the one field that crosses the process boundary, the two documents say different things.

The brief — which scope.md:7 calls "the authoritative design" and the plan at :8-9 says to read first — shows `{"cmd":"image.frameshm","args":{"handle":..,"w":..,"h":..}}`. The agwinterm plan defines the args as `{"images":[{"id","name":"Local\\...","slot","seq","width","height","stride","format","row","col","cols","rows"}]}` (context/agwinterm-dependency-plan.md:103-105) and opens the mapping with `MemoryMappedFile.OpenExisting(name, MemoryMappedFileRights.Read)` (:126).

These are not two spellings of one design. A Win32 HANDLE is process-local; its numeric value means nothing in the consumer unless the producer calls `DuplicateHandle` into the consumer's process, which requires knowing the consumer's PID and holding rights to it. The named-mapping shape is the workable one — so the brief is the wrong document here, and it is the document the plan tells the executor to trust. The Windows plan's own Task 10 (:229-232) says "create the named mapping", so the plan is right and the brief is stale; a reader who follows the plan's instruction to read the brief first gets the wrong shape.

A second gap in the same area, less certain: agwinterm's reader will "restrict accepted names to a fixed prefix in the `Local\` namespace" (dependency plan :130-131). The Windows plan's Task 10 never mentions a required prefix. If the exact prefix is not written into docs/specs/image-frameshm.md at agwinterm Task 1, the producer picks a name and is rejected at runtime with a validation error that looks like a bug.

Established by reading both documents; the DuplicateHandle point is Win32 semantics, not something I tested. Overturned if `handle` in the brief was always shorthand for the mapping name — in which case the fix is a word, but the word matters because ralphex codes against it.
findings.fix: Correct the brief's diagram to the named-mapping args before Task 10 starts rather than at Task 13, and add the exact `Local\` name prefix to the agwinterm Task 1 spec bullet so both sides pin the same string.

findings.title: Two slots plus an unsynchronised copying consumer does not make a torn read impossible
findings.body:
The dependency plan sets itself a hard constraint at :48-50: "Frames must never tear. A producer writing while the renderer reads is the default failure mode of any shared buffer; the design must make a torn read impossible, not unlikely." Its Technical Details at :198-203 then claims the two-slot scheme achieves that: "A frame in flight is therefore never the frame being read."

That claim does not hold for two slots without a back-channel. The consumer copies from the slot named by `ready`; nothing tells the producer when that copy finishes. Trace it: consumer reads `ready`=5 (slot A) and begins its memcpy. Producer fills slot B, publishes `ready`=6. Producer — free-running at browser paint rate, which is the entire premise — now needs a slot for its next frame, and the only other slot is A. It fills A while the consumer is still copying A. Torn read. A 1920x1080 BGRA frame is ~8 MB per copy, so the window is not narrow, and the failure gets *more* likely exactly when the producer is fast, which is the case the command exists for.

This is analysis of a written protocol, not of code — none exists yet — which is why my confidence is not higher. But the header already carries a slot count (:100-102), so the fix is cheap: three or more slots, or a consumer-written "currently reading" index the producer skips. It has to land in agwinterm Task 1, because the Windows plan's Task 10 (docs/plans/20260821-windows-port.md:229-231, "write BGRA into the inactive slot") codes against whatever that spec says, and "the inactive slot" is only well-defined if there is exactly one.

Overturned if the producer is to block until the consumer acknowledges, or is rate-limited below consumer speed by construction — neither is stated anywhere in either plan.
findings.fix: In agwinterm Task 1, either raise the slot count to three or add a consumer-published `reading` index to the header, and correct the Technical Details paragraph so the stated invariant matches the mechanism.

findings.title: Nothing sources the cell metrics and pane pixel size that Tasks 5, 8 and 9 all require
findings.body:
Task 5 requires "cell-span computation from pixel size and cell metrics" (:169-170), Task 9 requires a translation that "accounts for deviceScaleFactor and the pane's cell metrics" (:217-218), and Task 8 must render Chromium at some pixel size. I looked for where those numbers come from on Windows and found no supported source.

Established by reading: agwinterm's session-targeted control dispatch is `session.write/type/text/status` and `image.show/sixel/clear/frame` (ControlServer.cs:242-249). Grepping ControlServer.cs for `cell_width`/`cellW`/`CellSize`/`PixelWidth` returns nothing; `_cellW`/`_cellH` live only in Agwinterm.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:700 and are not exposed through the pipe. Grepping all of `src` and `native` for XTWINOPS (`14t`/`16t`/`18t`) returns nothing, so the client cannot ask the terminal for its pixel size either. Task 3's resize source (:139, console screen buffer info) yields cols and rows in character cells only.

The project's own record makes the query route worse, not better: issue yeroo/agwinterm#98 records, from a live VT tap, that "DSR/CPR (`CSI 6n`), DA1/DA2 — conhost responds on our behalf", and that an OSC 8 sent from a pane never reached the emulator. So a `CSI 14t` from inside a pane is likely to be answered by conhost or swallowed, never reaching agwinterm.

A workaround exists and the brief half-implies it: `image.frame` takes `cols`/`rows` (ControlServer.cs:444-445) and agwinterm scales the image to that cell span, so the producer can render at any resolution and let the terminal resample. But that costs text sharpness on a browser, and it is not what the plan says it will do. Either way this is potentially a third thing agwinterm must expose, alongside frameshm and key encoding.

Overturned if you intend to hardcode or configure cell metrics for v1, which would be reasonable — but the plan should say so, because an autonomous executor will otherwise go looking for a query that does not exist.
findings.fix: Decide and record where cell metrics come from — a new control verb, a config value, or "render at fixed resolution and let cols/rows scale it" — and add it to Task 4's client surface before Task 5 needs it.

findings.title: Mouse position is quantised to one character cell; there is no pixel-resolution mouse anywhere
findings.body:
Task 9 warns that "an off-by-one cell is a wrong click target", which frames the risk as translation accuracy. The real constraint is coarser: correct translation still lands the pointer on a lattice.

Established by reading: `SendMouse` at C:/Users/boris/source/agwinterm/src/Agwinterm.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:710-720 takes `(col,row)` from `CellAt` (:700), which is integer division of the pointer position by `_cellW`/`_cellH`, and emits `\x1b[<btn;col+1;row+1M`. Sub-cell position is discarded before the sequence is built, so it is not recoverable downstream by any amount of care in the port. `?1016` (SGR-Pixels) appears nowhere in agwinterm's `src` or `native` — I grepped for it and got nothing — and the emulator's mode handler covers only 1000/1002/1003/1006 (TerminalEmulator.cs:402-405). The brief's own quoted herdr metrics put a cell at 9x19 px.

What follows (my inference): in Chromium, every click, hover and drag snaps to a ~9x19 px grid. Hovering a 12 px link, placing a text caret mid-word, dragging a scrollbar or a column divider all become imprecise in a way no code in this repo can fix. That is a fair amount of "a real Chromium browser" (Overview, :5-6).

This is separate from the keyboard finding above and has a separate fix, which is why it is listed on its own. Overturned if cell-granularity pointing is acceptable for the intended use — plausible for reading and navigating, less so for the "page with a text input" and "heavy page" cases in Post-Completion (:294).
findings.fix: Either accept and record cell-granularity pointing as a known limitation in the brief and Task 9, or add `?1016` SGR-Pixels to agwinterm and to the pinned cross-repo dependency list.

findings.title: The zero-hit column contains modules that compile clean and silently behave differently on Windows
findings.body:
Goal item 1 asks whether the unix-reference count is a failing proxy, and names arboard and fontdue. I checked. The count itself is sound; the proxy does fail, in a specific and narrow way.

**Confirmed first, so you know what I cleared.** The 64/2/2 split and "19 of 22 with none" reproduce exactly. The "22 source files" counts only top-level modules — `pixel-core/src` actually holds 46 `.rs` files across `engine/`, `scroll/`, `selection/`, `surfaces/`, `tree/` — and re-running the same pattern over those 24 extra files returns zero hits, so widening the sample strengthens rather than weakens the claim. fontdue is genuinely free: every font is `include_bytes!("../../../assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf")` (paint.rs:775, menu.rs:356, text_input.rs:917, wrap.rs:139, tree/tests.rs:8), `engine/assets/fonts/` is a real directory and not a symlink, so there is no system font discovery to port — the usual Windows font-porting tax does not apply. arboard is used at exactly one call site (clipboard_image.rs:56) and is declared `arboard = { version = "3.6", features = ["wayland-data-control"] }` at engine/Cargo.toml:20; that feature gates a Linux-only optional dependency, which cargo excludes for a Windows target. I read this rather than building it, so it is the one item here I would still want a `cargo check` to confirm. native.rs degrades safely rather than breaking: `helper_path()` (native.rs:83-87) returns `None` without `NATIVE_SCROLL_HELPER`, so dropping upstream's Swift helper costs precise scroll and pinch-zoom, not a build.

**Where the proxy fails.** clipboard_image.rs:88-92 has zero unix-API references, compiles clean on Windows, and does the wrong thing: it rejects any path not starting with `/` or `~`, so `C:\Users\...` and `file:///C:/Users/...` both return `None`, and it resolves `~/` through `std::env::var("HOME")`, which Windows does not set. Pasting or dropping a file into the browser silently no-ops with no error path. Second instance: throttle.rs:71-73, `CpuThrottle::supported()` returns `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`, so the CPU throttle is inert on Windows; it is re-exported at lib.rs:58 and used by engine/mod.rs:40. That matters for Task 8's frame-budget measurement (:206), which will be taken with frame pacing that exists on macOS simply absent.

Both sit in the keep-unchanged 19, so fixing either collides with the constraint at :63-64 and Task 12's diff check at :260-261 — the same collision as the Task 2 finding, reached from a different direction. Overturned if clipboard file-paste and CPU throttling are both out of scope for v1, which is defensible but is currently unstated.
findings.fix: Add to Task 1's ➕ findings: clipboard_image.rs needs Windows path acceptance and USERPROFILE, and throttle.rs is inert on Windows. Record both as sanctioned exceptions to "keep 19 unchanged" now, so Task 12's diff check does not treat them as violations.

findings.title: Precedent: adding a control verb is a well-worn, repeatedly-accepted shape here, and the conformance constraint is now a CI gate
findings.body:
Reporting the sweep result so silence is not read as "no precedent exists". winterm-browser has no remote and three local commits, so there is no forge history for this repo; I swept agwinterm's, which has one (yeroo/agwinterm) with `gh` available.

**Supports the transport decision.** Adding a verb to the control API is routine and has been accepted repeatedly on its merits: #7 `feat(control): session.rename verb` (MERGED), #8 `feat(control): session.seen, sidebar read-back, version in ping` (MERGED), #68 `feat(control): font can target a specific split/scratch/quick pane` (MERGED), #201 `feat(control): resolve a session target by name, not just by id` (MERGED, 2026-08-20). `image.frame` itself was built for an external consumer, docxy, and is described in docs/agterm-gap-analysis.md:41 as delivered "out-of-band because ConPTY strips APC". So `image.frameshm` is not a novel shape for this project — it is the fourth or fifth instance of one it keeps choosing, for a reason that still holds.

**Strengthens the conformance constraint.** PR #195 `test(control-api): make the cross-product contract a gate` was merged 2026-08-18, three days before these plans. The dependency plan's rule at :43-46 — do not add `image.frameshm` to tests/conformance/control-api.json — is therefore not caution about a shared file, it is a recently-enforced CI gate that would fail agliteterm's build. That constraint is correctly stated and should not be softened during execution.

**Does not bear.** Upstream terminal-browser has no recorded position on Windows: README.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md mention neither Windows, Win32 nor WSL. scripts/install.sh:9-14 refuses non-Darwin/Linux, which the brief cites correctly, but that is a packaging fact rather than a decision anyone argued.

I have anchored this on plan line 58 only because it is the constraint the precedent bears on; the line itself also carries a small error, below.

findings.title: The shm-contract precondition is stated against Task 9 but consumed at Task 10
findings.body:
Constraints line 54-58 reads "If the contract is not ready when Task 9 starts, stop and say so rather than inventing a shape." The contract is not consumed at Task 9 — Task 9 is Interactive input (:212-222) and touches no shared memory. The precondition belongs to Task 10, which states it correctly itself at :226-227.

Established by reading the two task bodies. It matters only because of how these plans are executed: an autonomous runner reading the Constraints block literally can halt at the top of Task 9 for a missing precondition Task 9 does not need, and "stop and say so" is exactly the instruction it would follow. The same sentence also says "Everything up to and including the first-frame-on-screen milestone uses the file-based image.frame", which is right and identifies Task 8 as the boundary — so the off-by-one is in the task number alone.

Overturned if Task 9 was meant to be the number after a renumbering, in which case the whole block wants re-reading against the current task list.
findings.fix: Change "when Task 9 starts" to "when Task 10 starts" in the Constraints block.
